# Empirical Evaluation and Clinical Validation



## Study Design, Biomedical Cohorts, and Synthetic Ground-Truth Regimes

We evaluate the seven benchmarked architectures defined in Chapter 2 across twelve multi-view benchmarks: six real biomedical and clinical cohorts (`ADNI-MCI`, `MultiOmics` [TCGA-BRCA], `TCGA-KIRC`, `Heart`, `Diabetes`, and `mfeat`) and six synthetic generative regimes with known ground-truth latent coordinates $\mathbf{U}^*$ and feature supports $\mathbf{V}_m^*$ (@tbl-benchmark-cohorts). Every model is evaluated across three independent 70/30 stratified or random train/test splits (seeds $42, 43, 44$) across three `nsa_flow` quantile sparsity levels ($q \in \{\text{None}, 0.5, 0.8\}$, 756 train/test fits), plus 189 paired reruns with non-negative loadings on the three high-dimensional cohorts and a 1,025-configuration hyperparameter sweep on `ADNI-MCI` ($N = 1,084$, one seed). To prevent data leakage, all feature standardization (`StandardScaler`), column completeness filtering ($\ge 98\%$), and demographic covariate adjustments (Frisch–Waugh–Lovell residualization [@frisch1933partial; @lovell1963seasonal] of age, biological sex, and education inside `ADNI-MCI`) are fitted strictly within each training split and applied out-of-sample to the held-out test split.

In `ADNI-MCI` ($N = 1,084$) [@mueller2005; @jack2008alzheimer; @ADNI], Views 0–2 capture $382$ regional structural MRI features from the ANTsPyT1w/ANTsPyMM pipelines: the volumes of 160 hierarchical segmentation labels (View 0: cortical, subcortical, ventricular, white-matter and cerebellar labels), the volume-to-surface-area ratio of the same 160 labels (View 1; for a cortical label it tracks thickness, otherwise it is a shape index), and DiReCT cortical thickness averaged in each of 62 Desikan–Killiany–Tourville (DKT) cortical regions (View 2) [@avants2008symmetric; @avants2011reproducible; @tustison2014large; @desikan2006automated; @klein2012mindboggle; @stone2020longitudinal; @stone2024blast; @Marek2011; @smith2013functional], while View 3 comprises eleven neuropsychological scales (`ADAS11`, `ADAS13`, `ADASQ4` [@rosen1984new], `MMSE` [@folstein1975mini], `CDRSB` [@morris1993clinical], `TRABSCOR` [@reitan1958validity], `FAQ` [@pfeffer1982measurement], and four Rey Auditory Verbal Learning Test sub-scores `RAVLT_immediate`, `RAVLT_learning`, `RAVLT_forgetting`, `RAVLT_perc_forgetting` [@rey1964examen]). Following `Protocol B`, the three MRI views align with the cognitive battery during training, but test-set predictions are generated exclusively from structural MRI. In `MultiOmics` (`TCGA-BRCA`, $N = 822$) [@tcga2012breast] and `TCGA-KIRC` ($N = 467$) [@tcga2013kirc], mRNA expression ($p_1 = 200$), somatic copy-number variation ($p_2 = 150$), and RPPA proteomics ($p_3 = 150$) predict clinical Estrogen Receptor status and pathologic tumor stage, respectively.

## Global 12-Dataset Benchmark: Subspace Capacity vs. Single-Axis Interpretability

Across the $B = 12$ dataset blocks and seven architectures, block-averaged non-parametric Friedman [@friedman1937use] and Iman–Davenport [@Iman1980] omnibus tests differentiate the seven models on both the linear subspace probe ($\chi_F^2 =$ 15.31, $p =$ $1.80 \times 10^{-2}$; $F_F =$ 2.97, $p =$ $1.25 \times 10^{-2}$) and the multi-modal consensus probe ($\chi_F^2 =$ 13.77, $p =$ $3.23 \times 10^{-2}$; $F_F =$ 2.60, $p =$ $2.53 \times 10^{-2}$; Nemenyi Critical Difference $CD =$ 2.600 at $\alpha = 0.05$ [@Demsar2006; @Nemenyi1963; @benavoli2016should]). @tbl-global-leaderboard summarizes the global metrics across all seven models, accompanied by the Demšar Critical Difference diagram (@fig-cd-diagram), the multi-objective speed–accuracy and support–consensus Pareto frontiers (@fig-pareto-frontier), and the three-probe performance profile (@fig-three-probes).

Three empirical principles emerge from @tbl-global-leaderboard and Figures [-@fig-cd-diagram]–[-@fig-three-probes]:

1. **Multi-View Alignment Against Single-Matrix Factorization**: The leading mean Friedman ranks on the linear entrypoint probe are `NED` (3.04), `NEDPP` (3.21), `LEND` (3.29), `Flow-SiMR-V` (3.67), against `PCA` (5.46) and `NSAFlow-PCA` (5.29) (@fig-benchmark-uncertainty). On heterogeneous cohorts such as `mfeat` ($p = [76, 64, 6, 47]$) and `Shared+Private` ($p = [160, 60, 30]$), concatenated `PCA` reaches a linear score of 0.727 (`mfeat` accuracy) and 0.291 (`Shared+Private` $R^2$), against 0.972 (`NEDPP`) and 0.948 (`SiMLR`) for the best multi-view model. Over the 12 datasets (seeds averaged, Wilcoxon signed-rank against `PCA` with Holm adjustment, Appendix B), the linear score differs from `PCA` at $p < 0.05$ for 0 of 6 models (none).
2. **Coordinate Alignment and the Random Forest Axis Drop**: As established in @eq-subspace-invariance, ridge regression on $\mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m$ is insensitive to orthogonal or oblique column mixing $\mathbf{V}_m \mathbf{M}$, hiding the fact that dense `PCA` mixes distinct mechanisms across columns. With coordinate-splitting decision trees (`RandomForest`), `PCA` loses -0.044 on average across the 12 cohorts (Random Forest minus linear score), falling from 0.125 to -0.000 on the weak sparse factors of `NonnegPartsWeak` and from 0.152 to 0.044 on `ADNI-MCI` (71% lower). The smallest drops are `NED` (-0.014), `SiMLR` (-0.016).
3. **Operating Points and Feature Density ($q = 0.5$ vs. $q = 0.8$)**: @fig-operating-point-and-support shows the quantile threshold $q$ as a lens on feature support recovery without conflating scales on secondary axes. Across the 756 default-positivity fits, the mean linear score is 0.716, 0.718 and 0.718 at $q = \text{None}$, $0.5$ and $0.8$, and the mean Random Forest axis score is 0.689, 0.692 and 0.692; at $q = 0.8$, 57.8% of loadings are zero while 100.0% of the best linear score is retained. At $q = 0.5$, support recovery on the $50\%$-sparse `Linear` regime ranges from $F_1 =$ 0.500 (`PCA`) to 1.000 (`NSAFlow-PCA`), and reaches 0.875 on `NonnegParts` (`Flow-SiMR-V`). On the focal $20\%$-active modules, the best $F_1$ at $q = 0.8$ is 0.833 on `NonnegPartsWeak` (`Flow-SiMR-V`) and 0.806 on `Shared+Private` (`Flow-SiMR-V`).

## Clinical Neuroimaging in `ADNI-MCI` ($N = 1,084$): Predicting Cognition from MRI Alone and Attributing the Prediction

A primary clinical test of multi-modal representation learning is whether aligning structural neuroimaging with multi-domain cognitive batteries during training yields an anatomical basis that better predicts cognitive severity in new patients who have only undergone an MRI scan (`Protocol B`). Across $N = 1,084$ participants with Mild Cognitive Impairment, @tbl-adni-mci-summary compares all seven benchmark models on held-out MRI-only prediction of composite cognitive impairment (`CogPC1` $R^2$, after in-fold adjustment for age, sex, and education), single-axis Random Forest prediction, and mean ridge regression $R^2$ across all eleven individual neuropsychological scales (`ADAS11`, `ADAS13`, `ADASQ4`, `MMSE`, `CDRSB`, `TRABSCOR`, `FAQ`, and four `RAVLT` memory scales).

Comparing the unsupervised anatomical baselines against cognitive-aligned SiMR models in @tbl-adni-mci-summary and Figures [-@fig-adni-view-chord]–[-@fig-adni-scores] yields four findings:

1. **Supervising MRI Factor Discovery with Cognitive Batteries Improves Out-of-Sample MRI Prediction**: Unsupervised `PCA` on the $382$ structural MRI features explains $R^2 =$ 0.152 $\pm$ 0.004 of out-of-sample cognitive variance (`CogPC1`) on the linear probe and 0.044 on the single-axis Random Forest probe. Aligning the MRI projections with the 11-scale cognitive battery during training gives, for the four leading models (3-seed means $\pm$ SD), `NED` (0.209 $\pm$ 0.023), `NEDPP` (0.197 $\pm$ 0.016), `Flow-SiMR-V` (0.180 $\pm$ 0.035), `LEND` (0.170 $\pm$ 0.023); the best is +37.3% over `PCA`. The best single-axis Random Forest score is 0.154 (`SiMLR`), 3.5 times that of `PCA`. In the single-seed sweep the best configuration reaches 0.2552 (`LEND`) and the best linear-family configuration 0.2453 (`SiMLR`), against 0.1779 for `PCA`; mean prediction across all eleven scales reaches 0.121 (`LEND`) against 0.081 for `PCA` (+48.8%). These sweep peaks are maxima over many configurations on one split and are optimistic.
2. **Which MRI Features Carry the Prediction**: @fig-adni-neuroanatomy-flagship attributes the held-out `CogPC1` prediction of the non-negative $q = 0.85$ fit (all nine MRI columns, $R^2 =$ 0.204). Component 2 carries it in every MRI view: alone it gives $R^2 =$ 0.111 (volume), 0.211 (vol/area) and 0.148 (DiReCT thickness), against at most 0.031 for any other column, and only the vol/area column is not redundant with the rest (unique $R^2$ +0.054). Across 20 half-sample refits, the vol/area component-2 basis selects, in at least half of them, L entorhinal (DKT parcellation) (0.75), L inferior parietal (DKT cortex label) (0.75), R entorhinal (DKT cortex label) (0.75), L entorhinal (DKT cortex label) (0.75), L temporal lobe (0.75), L caudal middle frontal (DKT cortex label) (0.65): entorhinal, temporal-lobe and inferior parietal measures, the regions where atrophy is expected in prodromal Alzheimer's disease [@dickerson2009cortical; @jack2018nia]. DiReCT thickness tells the same story less clearly. Its first principal component explains 58% of the variance across the 62 regions (mean inter-region correlation 0.55), and consensus component 2 correlates 0.87 with subject-mean thickness, so hard-assigning each region to its largest structure coefficient places 2 / 60 / 0 regions on components 1 / 2 / 3: a display of the global factor, not of localisation (Panel B). The thickness basis itself is unstable under the default collapse penalty: it keeps two or fewer regions in 9 of 20 refits (median held-out $R^2$ 0.106). Non-negative region sums on positively correlated features necessarily correlate above the penalty's threshold of 0.3, so the penalty pushes those columns to single regions. With `collapse_weight = 0` the predictive thickness basis keeps a median of 9 regions (two or fewer in 1 refit), its median $R^2$ rises to 0.154, and its most frequent regions are L entorhinal (0.60), L supramarginal (0.55), L superior frontal (0.45), L inferior parietal (0.40), R entorhinal (0.40) (Panel D). No single thickness region replicates in more than 0.60 of refits, so the thickness map is a pattern, not a list of identified regions (`docs/audit/evidence/adni_global_factor_check.csv`). For reference, unthresholded non-negative fits are 67% sparse on the DKT view without rotation and 67% with Varimax, against 0% for dense `PCA`.
3. **Support-Shuffled and PCA-Rotated Score Controls**: To separate coordinate-level axis alignment and anatomical support localization from subspace capacity, two negative controls are evaluated across 3 seeds on `ADNI-MCI` (`adni_mci_axis_alignment_controls.csv`, `axis_alignment_control_metrics`): (i) a **PCA-Rotated Score Control** rotates the learned scores $\mathbf{Z} = [\mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m]$ by their in-fold principal-component eigenvectors, which leaves the linear probe unchanged (largest difference $2.83 \times 10^{-7}$) and lowers the single-axis Random Forest score for 2 of 5 models; (ii) a **Support-Shuffled Basis Control** permutes the rows of each $\mathbf{V}_m$ within its view, preserving sparsity, weight magnitudes and $\mathbf{V}_m^\top \mathbf{V}_m$, and lowers the Random Forest `CogPC1` $R^2$ for 5 of 5 models: `Flow-SiMR-V` (0.140 $\to$ 0.090), `LEND` (0.119 $\to$ 0.115), `NEDPP` (0.145 $\to$ 0.091), `NSAFlow-PCA` (0.060 $\to$ -0.057), `SiMLR` (0.112 $\to$ 0.056). Unshuffled Random Forest scores are 1.4–3.3 times that of `PCA`.
4. **Rank Selection, Component Identifiability, and Display Policy**: Evaluating latent rank selection via `select_rank` across 20 half-sample refits (`adni_rank_selection.csv`) reveals that component identifiability depends critically on rank $k$ and non-negativity. At $k = 3$ under non-negativity, component stabilities are 0.975 ($0.975$), 0.803 ($0.803$), and 0.996 ($0.996$). Component 2 is unstable ($0.803 < 0.90$) and therefore classified as **not identified** (`all_stable=False`). In contrast, at $k = 2$ under positivity, both components achieve full stability and identifiability (`all_stable=True`, stabilities 0.961 [$0.961$] and 0.997 [$0.997$]). Under signed estimation (`positivity="either"`), stabilities at $k = 3$ drop to 0.993 ($0.993$), 0.568 ($0.568$), and 0.792 ($0.792$), failing identification on components 2 and 3.
   * **Signed Displays Protocol**: Across all displays in this manuscript: (i) feature maps display only features whose 95% bootstrap confidence interval (from whole-pipeline refits in `loading_inference`) strictly excludes zero; (ii) named biomarker panels report features selected via Meinshausen–Bühlmann stability selection at threshold $\pi_{\text{thr}} = 0.80$ with expected false selections $E[\text{false}] \le 1.0$; and (iii) non-negative displays present hard-assignment OLEE loadings accompanied by the `loading_margin` certainty metric.

## Multi-Omic Oncology (`TCGA-BRCA`, `TCGA-KIRC`) and Patient-Level Clinical Attribution

To verify that the same architectural principles generalize beyond neuroimaging to molecular oncology and clinical tabular medicine, @tbl-real-cohorts-summary compares all seven models across the six real cohorts, @fig-multiomics-and-patient-attribution reports cross-cohort linear entrypoint scores (`pysimlr.plot_benchmark`), @fig-diabetes-top-features and @fig-heart-audit map reproducible feature-to-component structure (`pysimlr.plot_top_features` and `pysimlr.plot_feature_chord`), and @fig-nsa-v-interpretability displays the hard-assigned OLEE loadings $\mathbf{L}_m$ across `Heart` and `Diabetes` modalities.

In `MultiOmics` (`TCGA-BRCA`, $N = 822$), out-of-sample Estrogen Receptor classification accuracy on the linear entrypoint is 92.7% $\pm$ 0.7% (`Flow-SiMR-V`), 90.9% $\pm$ 1.7% (`LEND`) and 91.9% $\pm$ 1.1% (`NEDPP`), against 91.5% $\pm$ 1.8% for `PCA` (3-seed means $\pm$ SD); the sparse non-negative dictionaries $\mathbf{V}_m$, tri-modal feature chord, and view-level quality radar are examined in Appendix A. In `TCGA-KIRC` ($N = 467$), pathologic stage classification on the consensus embedding $\mathbf{U}$ is 61.0% $\pm$ 3.9% for `LEND` against 67.1% $\pm$ 1.5% for `PCA`. On compact clinical cohorts, `Diabetes` reaches $R^2 =$ 0.352 for `SiMLR` against 0.351 for `PCA`, and `Heart` reaches accuracy 0.848 for `NSAFlow-PCA` and 0.819 for `SiMLR`. @fig-diabetes-top-features, @fig-heart-audit, and @fig-nsa-v-interpretability show the stability-selected structure correlations, multi-view feature-to-component chord, and OLEE loadings $\mathbf{L}_m$ across `Heart` and `Diabetes`; while the linear entrypoint $\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}} = \mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m$ maps individual observations into the latent consensus space, the OLEE loadings $\mathbf{L}_m$ decompose individual patient profiles into exact additive risk attributions $c_{m,i,j,l} = x_{m,i,j} l_{m,j,l}$ without post-hoc Monte Carlo approximations [@Wachter_2017; @karimi2021algorithmic; @pearl2009causality]. Complete parameter sensitivity ablations—the $w \in [0.01, 0.95]$ trade-off curve, basis diagnostics, stability rank selection across $k$, and synthetic noise recovery—are in Appendix B.
